title: Ausgewählte Werke Bd. 1 (German, 1922)
author: Vladimir Solovyov
description: Ausgewählte Werke, Band 1 (Selected Works, Volume 1) of Vladimir Solovyov (Wladimir Solovjeff, 1853-1900), translated from the Russian into German by Harry Köhler (Stuttgart: Der Kommende Tag Verlag, 1922, Philosophisch-Anthroposophische Bibliothek, second printing). This volume contains Die geistigen Grundlagen des Lebens (The Spiritual Foundations of Life), first part, preceded by a biographical foreword. Solovyov, the leading Russian religious philosopher of the nineteenth century and theorist of Sophia (Divine Wisdom) and 'Godmanhood', wrote this work in the early 1880s as a meditation on the foundations of Christian life: prayer, almsgiving and fasting as the means of uniting the human with the divine, the person of Christ, and the Church as the body of the God-man. The anthroposophical publisher reflects Rudolf Steiner's admiration for Solovyov. It is a German-language source for Russian sophiology.
